Job Details:
Job Description:
Intel is shaping the future of technology to help create a better future for the entire world. Our work in pushing forward fields like AI, analytics, and cloud-to-edge technology is at the heart of countless innovations. With a career at Intel, you'll have the opportunity to use technology to power major breakthroughs and create enhancements that improve our everyday quality of life. Join us and help make the future more wonderful for everyone. Want to learn more? Visit our YouTube Channel or the link below.

Life at Intel

The Role and Impact
As a GPU Validation Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring the reliability and performance of Intel's industry-leading graphics processing units (GPUs). Your day-to-day responsibilities will involve defining and executing validation methodologies, debugging, and optimizing GPU features. By contributing to the development of cutting-edge validation infrastructure, you will help deliver products that meet rigorous performance, power, and quality standards. This position offers an exciting opportunity to innovate and make a tangible impact on Intel's graphics technology.

Business group
You will be part of Intel's Data Center Group (DCG), a team dedicated to delivering world-class GPU solutions for diverse applications such as gaming, AI, and high-performance computing. DCG focuses on driving innovation and supporting Intel's mission to shape the future of technology by creating advanced graphics architectures that power systems across desktop, mobile, server, and edge environments.

Key Responsibilities
- Define, develop, and execute validation methodologies for GPUs, focusing on interaction between media, display, and system-level features.
- Build and test emulation and prototyping models for GPU.
- Perform silicon debug to identify root causes and resolve functional and triage failures for GPU-related issues.
- Develop and maintain post-silicon validation infrastructure, including performance monitors, behavioral checkers, and test environments.
- Conduct validation testing to ensure performance, power, and area goals are met, leveraging hardware and software tools.
- Review design changes to assess their impact on validation plans, timelines, and tasks.
- Test interactions between GPU features using validation tools and infrastructure.
- Collaborate with architecture, design, board, platform, and manufacturing teams to optimize validation methodologies.
- Publish comprehensive GPU validation reports, summarize results, and communicate findings to relevant teams.
Qualifications:
You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience listed below would be obtained through a combination of your school work/classes/research and/or relevant previous job and/or internship experiences.

Minimum Qualifications:
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field with 4+ years of industry experience OR Master's degree in a relevant field with 3+ years of experience.
4+ years' experience in pre-silicon validation techniques, tools, and debugging.
4+ years' experience in C, C++, Python, and scripting for automation and validation tasks.
4+ years' experience in computer architecture and microarchitecture fundamentals.
4+ years' experience with emulation (preferably ZeBu/Palladium).
Preferred Qualifications:
Familiarity with PCIe standards and compliance processes.
Knowledge of GPU architecture.
Experience with FPGA prototyping, or acceleration platforms.
Experience developing validation protocols and strategies.
Experience with hardware debug tools such as logic analyzers, oscilloscopes, and in-circuit emulators.
Exposure to Design for Debug (DFD) tools and methodologies.
Familiarity with GPU artificial intelligence benchmarks, rendering concepts, and industry-standard APIs.
Strong communication and collaboration skills with cross-functional teams.

Join Intel's GPU Validation team and contribute to shaping the future of graphics technology through innovation and excellence. Apply now and take the next step in advancing your career.

Benefits at Intel
Our total rewards package goes above and beyond just a paycheck. Whether you're looking to build your career, improve your health, or protect your wealth, we offer generous benefits to help you achieve your goals. Go to Intel Benefits | Intel Careers for details of benefits available to you. Intel reserves the right to modify, change or discontinue benefit plans at any time in its sole discretion.

item.description:

Job Details:
Job Description:
Shape the Atomic Frontier of Semiconductor Innovation

At Intel Foundry Technology and Development (TD), we don't just participate in technology development; we engineer physical reality at the angstrom scale. We are seeking visionary, research-driven Ph.D. graduates in Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Materials Science, Electrochemistry, and Engineering to spearhead the next breakthrough in semiconductor manufacturing.

As a Wet Etch Module Development Engineer, you will operate at the intersection of fundamental chemical kinetics, interfacial surface science, and high-volume manufacturing engineering. You will pioneer atomic-layer selective etching, nanoscale surface cleans, supercritical and surface-tension-engineered drying, wet chemical formulations, and advanced single-wafer wet tool architectures to define the future of global computing.

What You Will Do:
Pioneer Next-Gen Process Architectures: Formulate and execute rigorous Design of Experiments (DOE) to invent, characterize, and validate novel wet etch, selective removal, and advanced chemical clean processes that power world-class transistor architectures (RibbonFET/GAA), backside power delivery networks (PowerVia), and high-density interconnect scaling
Lead Hardware and Module Co-Optimization: Collaborate with premier global semiconductor equipment suppliers and specialty chemical vendors to push single-wafer and batch wet processing capabilities beyond conventional fluid-dynamic and surface-tension limits, co-engineering custom dispense, megasonic, and chamber hardware solutions
Harness AI and Scientific Computing: Integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD), chemical kinetics modeling, statistical physics, and data science (Python, MATLAB, JMP, ML frameworks) to accelerate chemical formulation screening, surface defectivity reduction, and line-yield enhancement
Drive High-Impact IP: Translate complex chemical, electrochemical, and surface phenomena into high-value patents, trade secrets, and proprietary wet processing solutions that sustain Intel Foundry's technological leadership
Scale Science to Global Manufacturing: Bridge early lab prototypes and coupon-level studies to 300mm fab-scale ramp, seamlessly deploying high-throughput, defect-free wet processes across Intel's worldwide mega-fabs using our industry-leading Copy Exactly (CE) methodology
Why Join Intel Foundry TD?
Access to Unparalleled Technology: Direct, hands-on access to the industry's most advanced 300mm cleanroom facilities, state-of-the-art single-wafer wet processing platforms, and cutting-edge analytical surface characterization suites
Academic Rigor Meets Global Impact: The intellectual curiosity and depth of doctoral research combined with the scale, capital resources, and execution speed of an industry leader
Accelerated Technical Leadership: Direct mentorship and collaboration with Intel Fellows and Senior Principal Engineers on an accelerated path toward technical distinction
Comprehensive Total Rewards: Top-tier Ph.D. compensation packages, sign-on bonuses, annual performance bonuses, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP), equity/RSU grants, and full relocation assistance
Qualifications:
Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Requirements listed would be obtained through a combination of industry relevant job experience, internship experiences and or schoolwork/classes/research.
Minimum Qualifications:
Ph.D. in Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Materials Science and Engineering, Electrochemistry, Mechanical Engineering (Microfluidics/Transport Phenomena), Physics, or a closely related discipline (Degree completed or expected within 12 months)
2+ years of hands-on experimental research experience (e.g., doctoral dissertation, advanced wet chemical synthesis/etching, aqueous/non-aqueous solution chemistry, electrochemistry, surface functionalization, thin-film interface phenomena, or cleanroom wet bench processing)
Preferred Qualifications:
Demonstrated deep expertise in chemical reaction kinetics, selective wet etching, interfacial surface chemistry, corrosion/passivation mechanisms, or surfactant-assisted cleaning/drying mechanisms (e.g., Marangoni drying, supercritical (CO2), Surface modification (SMT))
Hands-on experience with advanced thin-film, surface, and chemical characterization techniques (e.g., Ellipsometry, AFM, SEM/TEM, XPS, contact angle goniometry, FTIR, TXRF, or ICP-MS)
Experience with automated fluidic systems, wet processing instrumentation design, single-wafer spin hardware, or experimental fluid dynamics/mass-transfer troubleshooting
Demonstrated experience utilizing Python, MATLAB, JMP, or Machine Learning for design of experiments (DOE), multivariate statistical analysis, or process automation
Strong publication record, conference presentations, or filed patent applications demonstrating systematic problem-solving in experimental chemical and materials science

Job Details:
Job Description:
The world is transforming - and so is Intel. Intel is a company of bold and curious inventors and problem solvers who create some of the most astounding technology advancements and experiences in the world. With a legacy of relentless innovation and a commitment to bring smart, connected devices to every person on Earth, our diverse and brilliant teams are continually searching for tomorrow's technology and revel in the challenge that changing the world for the better brings. We work every single day to design and manufacture silicon products that empower people's digital lives. Come join us and do something wonderful.

The Business Analyst- Data Center Systems supports the strategy and strategic programs function for Intel's Data Center Systems and Solutions team. Reporting to the Director of Strategic Programs, this role keeps the team's strategic work moving, compiling the data, running the logistics, and producing the first drafts that senior leaders build on.

The work spans systems strategy, customer engagements, executive reviews, and cross-group programs across DCG, and it will not always arrive in a predictable order. We are looking for someone who is comfortable handling a mix of planned and unplanned requests, can switch between domains quickly, and takes ownership of getting each task to done.
This is a growth role. You will start by running the logistics around the work and, as you build context, move toward contributing directly to analysis and strategy. Depending on your strengths and interests, you will have the opportunity to go deeper in areas such as systems strategy, market and competitive analysis, customer programs, or business planning.
Responsibilities:
Compile and analyze data from internal and external sources to support systems strategy, business cases, and executive decisions.
Produce documentation, reports, and summaries that are accurate, well-organized, and ready for leadership review.
Own logistics for reviews, customer engagements, and strategic deliverables: gather inputs, follow up with contributors, and assemble final materials on schedule.
Write first drafts of routine material, including status updates, briefing documents, meeting summaries, and presentation slides.
Provide light process support, about 15 percent of the role, maintaining dashboards, action trackers, and status reports where needed.
Handle ad hoc requests across the team, triaging priorities and keeping stakeholders informed on progress.
Build working relationships with contributors across DCG product, engineering, finance, and business teams.
Successful Candidate Profile:
Strong analytical skills, with the ability to turn raw data into clear findings.
Clear, concise writing and the ability to produce polished first drafts with minimal direction.
Highly organized, with attention to detail and reliable follow-through on deadlines.
Comfortable with ambiguity and shifting priorities, and able to manage several tasks at once.
Proactive and persistent in chasing inputs, with a professional approach to working with senior contributors.
Curious about data center technology, including CPUs, GPUs, servers, networking, and HPC and AI systems.

Job Description:
Intel Foundry Capacity and Strategic Planning is responsible for ensuring the right capacity is available at the right place, time, and cost to support customer commitments and business objectives across Intel's manufacturing network. This role drives strategic capacity planning across multiple technologies, sites, and planning horizons, enabling informed decisions that support growth, profitability, and operational excellence.

The successful candidate will partner closely with Factory General Managers, Manufacturing Leadership, Technology Development, Finance, Supply Planning, and Operations teams to develop executable capacity strategies, evaluate business tradeoffs, and influence critical investment and operational decisions.

Key Responsibilities
Lead long-range capacity planning, scenario development, and supply-demand analysis across Intel's manufacturing network.
Develop capacity strategies and recommendations that balance customer demand, factory capability, capital investments, and financial objectives.
Drive tradeoff analyses involving capacity, capital, technology transitions, factory space, and network optimization.
Partner directly with Fab Managers and manufacturing leadership to ensure plans are executable and aligned with factory realities.
Identify capacity risks and opportunities and develop mitigation strategies to support business objectives.
Prepare and deliver executive-level presentations, business cases, and strategic recommendations for senior leadership and executive reviews.
Translate complex analyses into concise and compelling business insights that drive enterprise-level decisions.
Lead cross-functional initiatives and influence stakeholders across Manufacturing, Technology Development, Finance, Supply Planning, and Foundry organizations.
Leverage AI, advanced analytics, and automation to improve planning efficiency, scenario evaluation, risk identification, and decision quality.
Drive adoption of AI-enabled planning and decision-support capabilities across the organization.
Behavioral traits:
Strong communication, executive storytelling, and presentation skills.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and data modeling skills.

This role is an On-site required position.
This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship.

Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Operations Research, Supply Chain, Business, Economics, or a related field.

The Solutions Architecture team sits within Marvell's Platform organization, which turns advanced silicon into deployable, customer-ready AI and cloud infrastructure. This team — the AI Solutions Lab — owns the validation layer that proves our platforms perform as promised, across compute, networking, and memory fabrics. Without it, Marvell could design great silicon but could never prove, at rack scale, that it performs the way customers expect — and hyperscalers don't buy chips on paper, they buy validated systems.

Day to day, the team runs AI benchmarking experiments that mirror real customer workloads, operates GPU/HPC lab clusters, validates Marvell's Teralynx switching and AI fabrics under production-like conditions, and builds live demos for trade shows — carrying platform programs from concept to production.

What sets this team apart is breadth of ownership: engineers here aren't limited to validating a single switch chip — they work across the full breadth of Marvell's AI platform portfolio, from Teralynx network fabrics to integrated optical platforms like co-packaged optics (CPO) and near-packaged optics (NPO), as well as emerging memory fabric products such as CXL and photonic fabric memory appliances.
